info.title: Iris Public API
info.description:
The public, versioned API of Iris. Authenticate with an API key:
`Authorization: Bearer iris_sk_…`. An owner or admin mints organization keys under
Organization → API keys, and any member mints personal keys under My agent access. Keys carry
scopes; a key without a route’s scope gets a 403 with `{ "error": "insufficient_scope" }`.
Each operation’s `x-iris-scope` names the scope it needs, or is null when any live key may call it.

Agent clients that cannot hold a key (Claude Desktop, claude.ai, ChatGPT) use OAuth 2.1 with
PKCE instead. They discover the authorization server from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`,
and send the access token the same way. Its scopes are the scopes above.

An OAuth token acts for the person who granted it, and a personal key for its owner. That
person’s current role and locations cap it. An owner or admin can turn a person’s agent access
off, alone or by role: their personal keys and OAuth tokens then get the 401 until it is back on.
Each operation’s `x-member-access` says what a MEMBER’s credential may do: `open` (call it),
`scoped` (call it, limited to the member’s locations), `sms_setting` (call it while the
member’s SMS setting is on, limited to their own clients at their locations) or `deny` (403 with
`{ "error": "insufficient_role" }`). An OWNER, an ADMIN and an organization key reach the
whole organization. `me_get` shows the person, role and locations behind the credential.

Every path is versioned. `v1` only ever grows: a breaking change ships as `v2`, and the
old version keeps serving with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers until it is retired.

send_at.description: When a `once` schedule sends. Required for `once`. A real calendar date-time ending in `Z` or an offset such as `-05:00`, for example `2026-11-01T09:00:00Z`. At most 40 characters.

rrule.description: An RFC 5545 rule such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0`, read in `timezone`. Required for `recurring`. Only these parts, each at most once: `FREQ` (`DAILY`, `WEEKLY` or `MONTHLY`), `INTERVAL` (1 to 100), `BYDAY` (1 to 7 distinct weekdays `MO` to `SU`, no number; on `DAILY` only with `INTERVAL=1`), `BYMONTHDAY` (`MONTHLY` only, 1 to 31 distinct days from 1 to 31 or -31 to -1), `BYSETPOS` (`MONTHLY` only, `1` or `-1`), `BYHOUR` (one hour, 0 to 23) and `BYMINUTE` (one minute, 0 to 59). Any other part, such as `COUNT` or `UNTIL`, answers 400. End a series with `ends_on`.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone `rrule` is read in

starts_on.description: The first day a recurring schedule may send (YYYY-MM-DD), from 2000-01-01 to 2100-12-31

ends_on.description: The last day a recurring schedule may send (YYYY-MM-DD), from 2000-01-01 to 2100-12-31 and not before `starts_on`

catchup_policy.description: Sends a recurring schedule missed, for example while Iris was down: `skip` drops them, `fire_once` sends only the latest.

throttle_per_minute.description: Stored for a planned limit on sends a minute, from 1 to 2147483647. Iris does not enforce it yet.

next_fire_at.description: The next send while the schedule is `scheduled`. Null on a `draft`.

status.description: `draft` sends nothing. `scheduled` sends at `next_fire_at`. `paused` starts no new run.

activation_warnings.description: Email setup that may keep mail from landing. Omitted when there is none.

cancelled.description: The enrollments of the run that were still active and are now cancelled
